newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Mandela to discuss role for S.Africa's PAC.
newsitem.headline: Mandela to discuss role for S.Africa's PAC.

text.p: President Nelson Mandela will meet the radical black Pan Africanist Congress this week for talks on the party's possible inclusion in South Africa's government of national unity, officials said on Sunday.
Mandela would meet PAC president Stanley Mogoba, presidential spokesman Parks Mankahlana told Johannesburg's independent Radio 702.
"President Mandela will meet the Reverend Stanley Mogoba to discuss the invitation the president has now issued to the PAC four times: to join the government of national unity," he said.
"The president has discussed the meeting with him already, but we do not know what his response is going to be."

Mandela invited the PAC to nominate members for senior government positions shortly after his African National Congress took power in South Africa's first all-race elections in 1994, but the party did not take up the offer.

The PAC campaigned mainly on a black supremacist platform and a demand for the return of land taken from blacks since the first white settlers arrived in 1652. It won only five of the 400 parliamentary seats, with 1.25 percent of the vote.
Mogoba stepped down last month as head of the Methodist Church in South Africa, which counts Mandela among its members, to lead the PAC, which he said needed him.

The party was founded in 1959 by ANC members dissatisfied with the high-profile role of whites in the movement and with the party's alliance with other groups, including the South African Communist Party.

Mandela's coalition cabinet currently includes the mainly Zulu-based Inkatha Freedom Party, but the National Party of former president F.W. de Klerk pulled out last year, saying the country could now benefit from a robust opposition.
